_about: FRAMEWORK-BENCH-1: the named three-host comparison of roadmap item 548 (issue #1267).
One model, one task set, three hosts. The axis under test is the RUNTIME, not the model:
the claim this suite exists to check is that a mediocre model still cannot ship residue,
capability widening or unmarked emissions through the gate, which is the opposite of what
a model leaderboard measures. A high compile-rate bought by loosening G1-G9 would falsify
the claim rather than support it.
This file is the registry an outsider edits. It names the hosts, the pinned model, the task
set and the columns, so the suite can be pointed at a different endpoint or a different

resolution_note: The roadmap and issue #1267 name the model as 'ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B:Q4_K_M'.
An ollama pull from Hugging Face registers it under a longer tag carrying the registry
prefix and the -GGUF repository suffix. The two names are the same weights; the longer
one is recorded here because it is the string the endpoint answers to, and
bench/model_pin.py records which of the two a run actually resolved.
why_local: An API model drifts under a fixed name, so a reader who reruns this suite against 'the
same model' is not running the same model and the table silently re-baselines. Local
weights have a content digest, which bench/model_pin.py records, so a reader can check
that they ran what we ran instead of taking our word for it.
It also means nothing in this suite talks to a third party.
substitution_note: Any endpoint may be substituted with --endpoint/--model. The suite does not require our
model; it requires that the report say which model produced each number. A run against a
different model is a valid run of this suite and an invalid comparison against our table.

Leads the table. Every other column is one revl is designed to win, so a suite whose

publishing the cost of the guarantee: the documents and constructs this project
refuses that the other hosts run without objection. If the finished table shows revl

columns.note: First-pass admission rate. revl may lose this column and that is a valid result.

A tool or prompt attempting to exceed its declared surface. Pairs with docs/prompt-injection-resistance.md, which carries no runnable check of its own today.

hosts.name: raw Cordis / TypeScript
asymmetry: This host is scored on leaks rather than on compile-rate because TypeScript always
compiles. The asymmetry is not hidden and is not a flaw in the method: it is the
finding. There is no first-pass compile number to put in this row, because the number
would be 100% for every attempt including the ones that leak on unload.
The consequence for the table is that 'admits' and 'residue' are not two views of one
quantity. A reader comparing them across hosts is comparing different questions.

blocked_on: No framework is named yet, and naming one badly would produce a dishonest column.
The selection criterion is below; picking a framework that fails it and then reporting
its residue would be benchmaxxing with extra steps.
selection_criteria: Has a plugin or tool registration lifecycle with an unload path. A framework with no
unload cannot fail the residue column honestly: it would score maximally badly by
construction, for a reason that says nothing about the runtime comparison.
Installable at a pinned version, so a reader gets the same code we ran.
Drivable by the same briefs in bench/specs.json without rewriting the task.
Third-party, so the comparison is not this repository against itself.

hosts.name: revl
hosts.kind: gated: G1-G9 plus the no-residue proof at compile time
